name: Educaplay
tagline: Browser tool for teachers to build quizzes, crosswords, matching games and other interactive classroom activities.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The activity types themselves are simple: multiple choice, fill in the blank, word search, crossword, matching, timeline ordering. An agent can generate a local web app with half a dozen of those templates plus an LLM step that turns pasted text into question sets, and that covers most of what a single teacher actually uses. What does not survive one session is the part around the activities: assigning them to a class, tracking who scored what, LMS handoff, and the shared library of activities other teachers already made. If you only need to build and project activities for your own students, the DIY version is fine. If you need student accounts and gradebook data, you are signing up for a much bigger build than a weekend.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you paste source material, pick an activity type, and it generates a playable quiz or word puzzle you can share as a static link.
requirements: An LLM API key in .env if you want auto-generated questions from pasted text
Somewhere to host static builds if you want students to open them on their own devices
whatYouLose: The public library of activities other teachers already authored
Student rosters, assignment flow and per student score tracking
Polished mobile behavior and accessibility work across many activity types
Someone else maintaining the drag and drop and touch handling for a dozen game formats
moatNotes: The teacher-authored activity catalog and the classroom integrations are the sticky parts, not the puzzle rendering.
whyPeopleStillPay: Teachers are not short on ideas, they are short on prep time. Paying means grabbing an activity someone already built for the same topic, assigning it in two clicks, and seeing results in a table without wiring anything. A self-hosted builder gets you the activities but hands back all the plumbing: hosting, links, results collection, and the nagging problem of it breaking on a student's phone during class.
notes: The puzzle formats are a weekend; the classroom plumbing is the actual product.
prompt:
Build a local-first interactive learning activity builder as a single web app. No accounts, no analytics, no cloud backend.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling
- Zustand for state
- Activities and generated content stored in localStorage, plus explicit JSON export and import
- Optional LLM generation via an OpenAI-compatible API, key read from OPENAI_API_KEY in .env, called from a tiny local Express endpoint so the key never ships to the browser

In scope, six activity types, each with an author view and a play view:
1. Multiple choice quiz, timed option, immediate feedback
2. Fill in the blank from a passage, author marks blanks by wrapping words in double braces
3. Word search grid, generated from a word list, click and drag selection
4. Crossword, generated from word plus clue pairs, simple greedy placement, no perfect density
5. Matching pairs, two column drag or click to pair
6. Ordering, drag a shuffled list into the correct sequence

Authoring:
- Sidebar list of activities, create, duplicate, rename, delete
- Per activity editor form driven by the activity type
- Paste a block of source text, hit Generate, get a draft question set or word list for the chosen type, editable before saving
- If no API key is set, hide the Generate button and say why in one line

Playing:
- Full screen play mode suitable for projecting, keyboard accessible
- Score shown at the end, retry button, no data leaves the machine
- Export any single activity as a standalone self contained HTML file that plays offline with no server

Out of scope, do not build: student accounts, rosters, gradebooks, LMS integration, a shared public library, multiplayer, leaderboards.

Deliverables: working dev server via npm run dev, a README with setup and .env.example, and three seeded sample activities so the app is not empty on first run.
